items.proposed_content: A Lefschetz pencil reframes the middle-cohomology problem for an even-dimensional smooth projective variety as cohomology of a family of hyperplane sections over P¹. Blowing up the pencil axis yields a proper map, and the Leray spectral sequence divides the target estimate among three explicit terms. For the difficult H¹ term, the source applies the Main Lemma to a certain quotient subquotient E of R^(d−1)f_*Q_ℓ: induction supplies hypothesis (i), an intersection form supplies (ii), and a theorem of Kazhdan–Margulis supplies (iii); duality then provides the opposite spectral bound.

items.proposed_content: Deligne's route replaces unavailable algebraic-cycle positivity with an analytic and monodromy-based weight mechanism: even tensor powers make local traces nonnegative, Grothendieck's trace formula turns global cohomology into pole control, big geometric monodromy identifies the relevant invariants, and unbounded powers erase the residual exponent error.

items.proposed_content: The curve case supports route plurality rather than one canonical proof: positivity can enter through elliptic-curve endomorphism degrees, surface intersection defect, Weil's determinant estimate for correspondence positivity, or the Rosati form on a Jacobian, while the Stepanov–Bombieri route records a different prerequisite boundary using only curve Riemann–Roch.

items.proposed_content: Weil cohomology separates the first three Weil-conjecture mechanisms from purity: trace and determinant compress fixed-point counts into a rational alternating product, the closed-point Euler product supplies integrality of the reduced numerator and denominator, and Poincaré duality supplies the functional equation; weight bounds are then the extra separator that prevents cancellation between cohomological degrees.

items.proposed_content: Finite-field purity and the global Hasse–Weil problem have different proof burdens: Deligne's theorem bounds the local Frobenius factors and thereby gives a convergence region for their Euler product, but meromorphic continuation and functional equation require completed global data and are approached, in known cases and in the general conjectural program, through automorphic or motivic identifications.
